extracted.intended_audience: actors, theatre practitioners, critics, and readers of dramatic criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative guidance and descriptive standards for stage acting in tragic / melodramatic roles, with emphasis on physicality, voice, truthfulness, pantomime, and staging as exemplified by Edwin Forrest's performances. Useful for actors, directors, and critics assessing theatrical portrayal and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensity of suspense / audience physical reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece repeatedly notes scenes where the 'intensity of suspense' produces visceral audience reactions (e.g., 'his heart beat with remittent throb', spectators with 'scarcely ever many dry eyes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build and sustain suspense so that the audience experiences a physical, emotional response; use pacing, tableau, and concentrated dramatic behavior to produce 'a silence that was absolute' and painful suspense when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convincing parental love and tenderness
rubrics_metrics.description: Portrayals of parental affection must be genuine and moving (example: Virginius taking Virginia in his arms and the passage that makes 'scarcely ever many dry eyes in the theatre').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intimate gestures, fond looks, and tender vocal tones to communicate filial love; small physical details (kisses, holding the head) should convey deep feeling without caricature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid and credible emotional transitions (tenderness to violence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to move from 'blistering and disdainful apostrophe' or tenderness to sudden violent action (e.g., Virginius changing from paternal love to seizing a knife and slaying his daughter) in a way that feels psychologically authentic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage and act transitions so that key beats (discovery of a prop, inner reverie, sudden resolution) are clearly motivated; small preparatory gestures (stealing a glance at a knife, passing it hand-to-hand) make abrupt acts plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powerful stage tableau and commanding presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating tableaux and poses that hold the audience—'the imperial front', 'bearing Virginia on his arm', 'the tableau caused a silence that was absolute'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose visual moments (posture, grouping, lighting, stillness) that produce concentrated attention; cultivate a bearing that reads well across the house and can 'throw a thousand invisible tendrils' around other characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocal clarity, strength, and moral authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of 'strong, lucid, cutting tones' and a 'kingly voice' that can break the spell of silence and impart moral weight to lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train voice for projection, clarity, and tonal variety; deliver moral or climactic speeches with authority, varied pacing, and precise enunciation to maximize rhetorical impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and rhetorical power of speech
rubrics_metrics.description: The actor's speech can turn the stage into a pulpit—lines with deep moral meaning should be delivered so the audience feels their weight ('the next passage of the play had a moral meaning deep enough, and was represented with a truth and power grand enough, to turn the stage for the time being into a pulpit').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize moral clarity in declamation; make ethical stakes explicit through tone and emphasis rather than mere gesture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and originality combined (no falsifying fundamentals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art must 'not falsify any fundamental principle or fact, but is free to modify and add'—a balance of accurate truth-to-life with artistic invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground characterization in real observation and fact; allow imaginative augmentation for theatrical effect but avoid contradicting essential truths of the character or situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity through immersion and study
rubrics_metrics.description: Forrest's embodiment came from 'recall[ing] all his observations' and 'patiently studied their characteristics from all other available sources' (meals, sleeping in tents, adopting habits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors should research and, where possible, immerse in real-life experience of the role's culture/condition to capture mannerisms, breathing, gait, and vocal qualities authentically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete physical identification with role
rubrics_metrics.description: 'He was completely transformed... seemed Indian in every particular, all through and all over, from the crown of his scalp to the sole of his foot.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fully commit to costume, makeup, movement, and micro-gestures so the performance reads as an organic whole rather than an overlay of acting choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of natural imagery and culturally-appropriate metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: Speeches stocked 'with fresh suggestions and images of nature' that resonated with audiences because they were 'drawn direct from the great objects of the universe.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating speech rhythm and image, draw on motifs authentic to the character's worldview (landscape, seasons, animals) to awaken audience recollection and sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject choice that connects with audience sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Indigenous or native subjects were 'indigenous, and thus came home to the American heart' and tapped a 'wide-spread sentimental interest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select or emphasize themes and subjects that resonate with communal memory or national sentiment to enlist broad audience sympathy (while being mindful of historical accuracy and ethics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pantomime and by-play as a source of truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of 'by-play of pantomime so true to Indian nature' to fill moments and make behaviors convincing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ restrained, character-specific pantomime to express inner state in pauses or hesitations instead of relying solely on speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and precision of movement and posture
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed attention to carriage, foot placement, breathing, and 'the sudden muscular movements, the repressed emotion, the peculiar mode of breathing' are praised as authentic traits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refine small physical details—breath, stance, foot angle, head carriage—so movements are economical, easily readable, and true to the character's physiology and culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathos must be genuine, not mechanical
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Pathos is the one particular affection that knows no deceit... Only a disagreeable mockery of it can thus come.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mechanical tears or contrived gestures; cultivate inner feeling and vocal subtlety so pathos arises spontaneously and is sensed as truthful by the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice as principal vehicle for pathos (pathos without tears/gesture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metamora's pathos is described as 'a pathos without tears or gesture... almost solely a pathos of the voice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop tonal and inflectional control to convey grief and tenderness through voice alone when the character's culture or temperament demands restraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorable phrasing and public effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines and modes of delivery that enter public speech ('Metamora cannot lie' circulating among boys) indicate a performance's cultural penetration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor clarity and distinctiveness in key lines so they register memorably; physical and vocal signature choices can create quotable moments that reinforce character identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of props as dramatic instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Props (knife, urn, eagle's feather) are functional triggers in scenes: the sight of a knife precipitates decisive action and meaning ('At the sight of this providential instrument an electric change passes over his face').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate props into the actor's inner life and stage business so that their discovery and manipulation feel inevitable and dramatically charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing physical/melodramatic display with sincerity

rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a role legitimately demands muscularity or heightened physicality, perform it with truthful conviction rather than exaggeration—physical heroism must serve veracity, not mere spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing, inflection, and tonal variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous passages stress shifts in tone—'rich, subdued undertone, waxing intenser,' 'a crisp tone of voice', 'aerial falsetto'—as essential to conveying vision, irony, menace, or tenderness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work precise timing of crescendos, sudden tonal changes, and subtle inflections to shape audience feeling and to delineate mental states; small changes in tone can render scenes profoundly moving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of contrast to heighten effect (calm vs fury)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pathos in Metamora is 'finely set off by the contrast that immediately foreran it, its soft, sad shades following a scene of lurid fury and grandeur.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure scenes and performance beats to juxtapose extremes—stillness after frenzy, tenderness after violence—to amplify emotional resonance.
